parts.name: Frame
parts.description: A tubular-steel frame that, in Honda's words, 'holds the engine in three places.' The tube layout shown is representative.
parts.function: The backbone of the motorcycle. It joins the steering head, the engine, the swingarm pivot and the rear shocks, and sets the steering geometry and wheelbase.

parts.name: Engine Mounting / Hangers
parts.description: The brackets, hanger plates and bolts that attach the engine to the frame. Honda states the frame holds the engine in three places.
parts.function: Locate the engine in the frame and pass loads between them. Because the engine is part of the chassis structure, these joints also contribute to frame stiffness.
parts.verificationNote: The three mounting locations are confirmed by Honda. Their positions, hardware, part numbers and torque values are not yet verified for 2026 CMX500A, so no mount geometry is drawn.

parts.name: Swingarm
parts.description: The pivoting rear fork that holds the rear axle. In Honda's catalog it sits under the frame group.
parts.function: Lets the rear wheel move up and down while keeping it aligned. The twin rear shocks control that motion.

parts.name: Side Stand
parts.description: A fold-out kickstand. It is drawn here in the retracted position.
parts.function: Supports the parked motorcycle. On many Honda models a side-stand switch also stops the engine if a gear is selected with the stand down; that switch is not yet verified for 2026 CMX500A.
